title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: scope policies to users with adaptive scopes
summary: The briefing needs a small permissions correction before publication: it presents two role groups as mandatory even though Microsoft documents other roles with the same configuration permissions. The roadmap facts, licensing model and principal controls are supported; two navigation paths need minor completion.

claims.claim: Scope Manager is included in the six built-in role groups named in the briefing.
claims.quote:
- Compliance Administrator
- Compliance Data Administrator
- Organization Management
- Records Management

- Communication Compliance Admins

claims.claim: Configuring Communication Compliance policies needs the Communication Compliance or Communication Compliance Admins role group.
claims.quote:
Members of the following roles have the same solution permissions included with the Communication Compliance Admins role group:

- Microsoft Entra ID Global Administrator

claims.fix: Replace the policy-permissions clause with 'the Communication Compliance and Communication Compliance Admins role groups can configure Communication Compliance policies.' This preserves the documented permission without falsely making membership of those two groups mandatory. See https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-permissions.

claims.claim: The portal route to adaptive policy selection is Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Choose users and reviewers > Choose users and groups > Select adaptive scopes.
claims.quote:
On the Choose users and reviewers page:

    1. In the Choose users and groups section, select one of the following options:

claims.claim: A supported automation operation for applying adaptive scopes to Communication Compliance policies is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: communication compliance adaptive scopes PowerShell IncludeAdaptiveScopes Set-SupervisoryReviewRule; "Communication Compliance" "adaptive scopes" "API". Opened New-/Set-SupervisoryReviewRule and setup guide: parameter descriptions remain placeholders; setup requires the portal.

claims.claim: The PowerShell reference lists IncludeAdaptiveScopes without describing its behaviour.
claims.quote:
### -IncludeAdaptiveScopes

> 
> Applicable: Security & Compliance

{{ Fill IncludeAdaptiveScopes Description }}

claims.claim: The setup guide directs administrators to manage Communication Compliance policies in the portal rather than PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can't use PowerShell to create and manage Communication Compliance policies. You must use the Communication Compliance solution.

claims.claim: Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope is the portal route for defining a scope query.
claims.quote: On the Adaptive scopes page, select + Create scope.
claims.fix: The route correctly opens creation but stops before the query controls. For an advanced-query route, use 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope > Full directory > scope type > Advanced query builder', where scope type is Users or Microsoft 365 Groups. The cited adaptive scopes page documents those choices; keep the existing Scope Manager note.

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType> -RawQuery <String> creates a scope using an advanced query.
claims.quote:
New-AdaptiveScope
    -Name <String>
    -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType>
    -RawQuery <String>

claims.claim: The New-AdaptiveScope reference describes retention policies, while the adaptive scopes overview also documents Communication Compliance use.
claims.quote: Adaptive scopes (or static scopes) are used in retention policies and retention label policies.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Scope details opens scope membership.
claims.quote: From the Details flyout pane, select Scope details.
claims.fix: Include the flyout heading: 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Details > Scope details', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes. This is an omitted heading, not a missing selectable navigation step.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity <ComplianceRuleIdParameter> -State Added retrieves current adaptive scope members.
claims.quote:
Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity "US Finance Users" -State Added
```

This example retrieves the current members of the adaptive scope US Finance Users.

claims.claim: Query changes can take up to five days to become effective and appear in Scope details.
claims.quote: adaptive scope query changes can take up to five days to become effective and reflected in the scope details view of the Adaptive Scopes page.

claims.claim: The membership cmdlet's default page returns at most 10,000 members.
claims.quote: For larger scopes, only the first 10,000 current members are included, and the first object in the response contains metadata with a watermark that can be used to request subsequent pages.

claims.claim: Passing the returned Watermark to PageCookie retrieves the next membership page.
claims.quote: To retrieve the next page, pass the Watermark value to the PageCookie parameter in your next invocation of the cmdlet.

claims.claim: State Added in Scope details identifies current members.
claims.quote: Review the State column in the list that shows Added for members within the adaptive scope or Removed if the member was previously in the adaptive scope but removed now they no longer match the scope query.

claims.claim: Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users is the documented role-group membership route.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, select Roles and groups, then select Role groups in the left navigation pane.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds the identified user to a role group.
claims.quote:
Add-RoleGroupMember
    [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter>
    -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter>

claims.claim: The Communication Compliance and Communication Compliance Admins role groups can configure policies and settings.
claims.quote: | Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes | No | No | No |

claims.claim: An adaptive scope is a reusable configuration element usable by Communication Compliance, retention and auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: When you create a communication compliance policy, a policy for retention, or an auto-labeling policy, you can add an adaptive scope for your policy.

claims.claim: Changing a shared scope's query changes the membership targeted by policies using that scope.
claims.quote: As a reusable configuration element, the same adaptive scope can be used for other compliance policies.

claims.claim: Administrative units can restrict investigators to a geography or department's user activity.
claims.quote: a global company that has subsidiaries throughout the world might want to create an admin unit that provides a German scope for investigators so that they only see user activity for German users.

claims.claim: Role group permissions can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After configuring your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.
